question.problem: Consider the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/72fbab5188e56a706bdf4d7140195877e8502427612b75f282dfc925f9147dd1.svg) and the quadratic curve $\mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{x} = 1.$ Given that $A$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_1=3$ and $\lambda_2=1,$ find the principal axes of the curve.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve 

$$
\mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{x} = 1
$$

are the vectors that give an orthonormal eigenvector basis for $A.$ Let's now find these eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_1=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-3I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/9d5eb1eefa424b5ff9c333542b4f716e7143c373acc117717468e1c8001a734f.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_1$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_1  \| = \sqrt{2},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/121a999cbd8cae4ff350fd293f6e3868ed67cf37b2124d275cbad64247520abe.svg)

- For $\lambda_2=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-1I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/6be78db327451dd23356dd9aa4e642cf82d46cbbd38a59116b646845acea464c.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_2$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_2  \| = \sqrt{2},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/3a400cd54548081008777aaded28248665cd2504e7d49aabedb110255a62a124.svg)

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\qquad$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/d77c04016cbb3353a54b35e7881a8895159bdad96147d36a5879e7e38b8de88f.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/5e54dea73a2277654f1f8a2a5b70e09030d5f8e395f99322948b30293cb5a0c2.svg)
